rounds.proof_sketch: Original: tid==0 writes V=shared_sum[0]/element_count to output[batch_idx]. Mutated: tid∈{1,...,255} all write identical value V to output[batch_idx]. CUDA serializes concurrent writes to same address; since all 255 threads write same value, final result is identical to original.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes which threads write to the output array, but does not change the value being written. In the original code, thread 0 writes shared_sum[0]/element_count. In the mutated code, threads 1-255 all write the exact same value to the same memory location. After the final __syncthreads() in the reduction loop, all threads see the same shared_sum[0] value. CUDA handles concurrent writes to the same address by selecting one winner, but since all 255 writers have the same value, the result is deterministically correct. This makes the mutant functionally equivalent regardless of input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The mutation swaps tid==0 with tid!=0 for a write operation, but since all threads compute and write the same value (shared_sum[0]/element_count is data-independent of tid at write time), the observable output is always identical to the original.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing CUDA kernels, mutations to thread selection conditions for writes should be paired with checks for whether the written values are thread-dependent. A truly distinguishable mutation would need to change either the value being written or result in no write occurring at all.
